pages.text: A swan lady stepped softly through the gate. Dad bowed. Kota quickly hid behind a post.
"Who's that little one?" She looked around. Kota hugged the post and peeked out, then blushed and hid again.
Even at dinner, Kota stayed behind Dad. "I want to say hello... but my mouth won't open." Kota gripped his sleeve.
Dad sat facing Kota. "Shall we play echo? When I bow, you bow!" Dad bowed first; Kota copied without thinking.
"Now add a smile." Dad smiled and bowed. Kota smiled and bowed, too. "Oh, the smile comes by itself!"
"A greeting is an echo. Send it, and it comes back." From the porch, Kota called into the valley, "Smile and Bow!" The valley returned, "...Bow!"
In the morning, Kota stood before the swan, hands together: smile, bow! She bent her long neck and returned it. "What a lovely greeting!" Kota's tail shot up.
"It came back like an echo!" Kota hopped. Dad and Kota slapped palms together.
Returning from a walk, the swan entered the gate. Kota faced her and counted aloud. "One, face each other! Two, smile! Three, bow!" Returned greetings filled the yard.
That evening, Dad sat Kota on his lap. "A greeting coming back is a heart coming back." "Tomorrow, Smile and Bow!" Kota bowed to Dad, too.
